summary: Buffalo plays Monday night in Los Angeles without WR Joshua Palmer and DT Ed Oliver, with DJ Moore a game-time call; on Thursday, Denver may again be missing both starting corners against Seattle, and no TNF props are posted yet.

NFL|00-0037840|rec.note: Since Nacua returned, Williams has drawn about a fifth of the targets with 16 catches over two games on a 76% snap rate. Buffalo gives up a lot of receiving production to backs.

detail.availability: Not on the Rams injury report.
detail.role: Played about 76% of snaps over the last two games and out-touched Corum 47 to 14, with roughly a 20% target share, third-highest among backs.
detail.matchup: Buffalo ranks near the bottom in fantasy points allowed to backs as receivers and gives up about 40 receiving yards per game to RBs. It also plays mostly zone, which tends to leave short check-downs open.
detail.script: As a small home favorite in a high-total game, the Rams should run plenty of plays, and Stafford has been throwing about 40 times per game.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over around 60%, above the 52.4% break-even.
detail.experts: One props preview backs his receiving yards over, citing his route share; another backs his rushing yards under because Corum shares the carries.

NFL|00-0039498|pat.note: With implied Rams points near 29 indoors, three touchdowns are plausible, but no news specifically affects his extra-point volume, and the Rams defense has held opponents to few red-zone drives.

detail.script: Implied team total is about 28.75 with the total up to 54.5; Buffalo is without DT Ed Oliver.
detail.conditions: Indoors, so kicking conditions are not a factor.

NFL|00-0039751|rec.note: His 2026 role is thin: three targets all season, a low target rate per route, and fewer snaps than Mumpfield. With Nacua, Adams and now Parkinson healthy, his snaps are even less secure.

detail.availability: Missed Week 2 with a quad injury; not on this week's report.
detail.role: Season totals are about two catches on three targets, and he has played fewer snaps than Mumpfield. He had one catch on two targets in Week 4.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 58.5%, which seems to rest on last season's larger role.

NFL|00-0026498|pyd.note: Buffalo's pass defense is short-handed: DT Ed Oliver is out and nickel Dee Alford is questionable. Stafford has thrown for 300 or more yards in three straight games.

detail.availability: Healthy; Adams's missed Thursday practice was a rest day.
detail.role: He has the highest pass volume in the league, with 106 attempts over the last two games, and Nacua is back.
detail.matchup: Buffalo allows about 274 passing yards per game. It plays zone most of the time, though, and Stafford has graded poorly against zone this year.
detail.script: In a high-total game, he is unlikely to be asked to protect a big lead.
detail.market: Current previews quote 275 to 285.5 against the packet's 279.5, and Kalshi is near a coin flip.
detail.experts: Experts are split: one model leans over because of Buffalo's yards allowed, while an NBC analyst leans under, citing Stafford's struggles against zone and the possibility of a run-heavy plan.

NFL|00-0040590|rec.note: He has played more snaps than Whittington this season and drew three targets in Week 4, but Parkinson's return could cut into three-receiver sets. Nothing clear beyond the numbers.

detail.role: He has played about half of the team's snaps this season, ahead of Whittington.

NFL|00-0035537|rec.note: He is still Buffalo's passing-down back, with four catches in Week 3 and two in Week 4. Palmer being out thins the receiving group, but no news points to more targets for him specifically.

detail.availability: Not on the Bills injury report.
detail.role: He has kept the receiving-back role since returning from a hamstring injury in Week 3.
detail.script: As road underdogs facing a strong Rams pass defense, Buffalo may throw more on passing downs.

NFL|00-0039901|rec.note: Palmer is out. Moore missed Thursday and Friday but practiced limited Saturday and is a game-time call; Coleman's volume jumps only if Moore sits.

detail.role: He ran a route on about 80% of dropbacks with Moore off the field and has two six-catch games in the last three weeks.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 37.5%, which appears to assume a full receiver group.
detail.experts: Several previews name Coleman as the main beneficiary if Moore sits.

NFL|00-0033110|rec.note: Starting TE Parkinson practiced fully Friday and Saturday and has no game status, so Higbee goes back to TE2 after starting while Parkinson was out.

detail.role: His five catches last week came with Parkinson inactive. McVay said Parkinson's reps may be managed, which leaves some room for Higbee.
detail.matchup: The Rams' high-volume passing game is unchanged, but Buffalo is about average against tight ends.

NFL|00-0038933|rec.note: Kincaid ran routes on only about half of dropbacks in Week 4, a season low. The Rams have allowed about 21 yards per game to tight ends, the fewest yards per target in the league.

detail.role: He has three catches over the last two games, and Knox is taking some of his snaps. Brady said he wants Kincaid more involved.
detail.matchup: The Rams have held Kittle, Likely and the Eagles' tight ends in check.
detail.experts: One props preview backs his receiving yards under 57.5 for these reasons.

NFL|00-0037840|td.note: He is the lead back near the goal line and scored twice late last week, but Corum takes about 38% of the carries and the market already prices him near 59%.

detail.role: He handled most of the touches over the last two games, but Corum has 33 carries on the season.
detail.market: His shortest anytime price is around -142, about 59% implied.

NFL|00-0039075|td.note: Nacua is healthy and back as the focal point, with 12 targets last week against a Bills secondary missing corners, but nothing points to a specific red-zone edge beyond the market's roughly 52-54%.

detail.availability: Back from a hip injury that cost him two games; not on this week's report.

NFL|00-0037248|td.note: Allen has scored a rushing TD in every game and handles much of the goal-line work, which limits Cook's scoring chances, but no source confirms the exact inside-the-5 split.

detail.role: Allen keeps getting goal-line carries even with Cook on the field.
detail.matchup: The Rams allow about 3.8 yards per carry to backs and few rushing TDs; one preview says they have allowed none to backs.

NFL|00-0034857|td.note: Allen has nine red-zone carries, six inside the 10, and more inside-the-five carries than Cook. He has scored a rushing TD in every game this season.

detail.role: He is Buffalo's de facto goal-line runner.
detail.matchup: The Rams allow touchdowns on about 58% of opponents' red-zone trips.
detail.market: Kalshi is at 52.5%, well above the app's 43.7%; books range from about even money to -115.
detail.experts: Two separate previews back his anytime TD, both citing his goal-line carries.

NFL|00-0031381|td.note: Buffalo is 29th in TD rate allowed to outside receivers and is missing corners, but Adams's target rate drops sharply with Nacua back, which leaves him relying on touchdowns.

detail.availability: His missed Thursday practice was rest; he practiced fully Friday and Saturday.
detail.matchup: Buffalo has allowed a 9.3% TD rate to outside receivers.

NFL|00-0038543|rec.note: Denver's top corners Surtain and Moss both missed Week 5 and may sit again on the short week, but neither is ruled out yet; check Denver's estimated practice reports.

detail.availability: No injury listing for Smith-Njigba, and he has played every recent game. It is Monday, so no Week 6 practice report exists yet.
detail.role: He led Seattle in targets in Week 4 on only 22 Darnold attempts, then drew 8 targets in Week 5. Shaheed has had little volume, so the targets stay concentrated on him.
detail.matchup: Surtain hurt his ankle in Week 4, was projected to miss about two games, and sat in Week 5. Moss (ribs) also sat. On a Thursday turnaround, backups Abrams-Draine and Barron are the likely starters.
detail.script: The game projects as close, with Seattle a slight road favorite, so there is no strong pull toward running out the clock.
detail.conditions: Forecast wind around 14 mph with gusts near 21 and a 40% chance of rain could trim the downfield passing more than the short catches.
detail.market: There is no Kalshi price. The total has drifted from 42.5 at open to 41.5.
detail.experts: No Week 6 previews of this prop were out as of Monday.

NFL|00-0034348|rec.note: Denver's pass volume was thin in Week 5 and wind and rain are forecast, but WR Pat Bryant's ankle injury could send more targets to Sutton, so the reasons cancel out.

detail.role: Sutton caught 2 of 3 targets, one for a TD, as Nix threw only 27 times in a run-leaning win. Waddle splits the top targets with him.
detail.script: Denver is a small home underdog in a low-total game, and Payton has publicly flagged third-down offense as a problem.
detail.conditions: The forecast calls for about 14 mph wind and a 40% chance of rain.

NFL|00-0037545|recyd.note: Shaheed's role is small behind Smith-Njigba, but Denver's backup corners make his deep shots more viable. Wind could cut into that, so there's no clear edge.

detail.role: He had 1 catch on 3 targets in Week 4 and added a 28-yard rushing TD. He had little production through the first three games.
detail.matchup: Surtain and Moss are both likely out, leaving reserves on the outside.
detail.conditions: The forecast wind of about 14 mph, gusting to 21, works against long throws.

NFL|00-0039732|ptd.note: Denver's passing game was weak in Week 5 and WR Bryant is hurt, but Kalshi already prices the under at about 67%, so the extra news adds little.

detail.role: Nix went 16 of 27 for 123 yards with 1 TD in the 23-17 win over the Chargers, and Dobbins handled the goal-line work.
detail.conditions: Wind and possible rain are in the forecast.
detail.market: Kalshi has the over at 33%, and the total has slipped to 41.5.

NFL|00-0034869|ryd.note: There is nothing new on Darnold's running. He had one 5-yard scramble in Week 5.

detail.role: He carried once for 5 yards in the Week 5 loss to San Francisco.

NFL|00-0036158|ryd.note: Dobbins is the clear lead back with 18 carries in Week 5, and wet, windy weather may tilt Denver toward the run. Seattle's strong front and an underdog script offset that.

detail.role: He had 18 carries for 68 yards and a TD against the Chargers.
detail.script: Denver is a home underdog of about 1.5 to 3 points in a low-total game.
detail.conditions: A 40% chance of rain and about 14 mph wind could favor the ground game.

NFL|00-0038797|car.note: Charbonnet is expected to stay out but it's not final, and Holani has shared work. Wilson had 20 carries in Week 5 but also lost a fumble.

detail.availability: Macdonald said Charbonnet will not be activated for Thursday. Jadarian Price missed Week 4 and his Week 6 status is unclear.
detail.role: Wilson had 22 touches in Week 5 (20 rushes) and lost a fumble. Holani had 7 carries in Week 4.
detail.conditions: Rain and wind in the forecast could push Seattle toward the run.

NFL|00-0038543|recyd.note: Smith-Njigba had 102 yards in Week 5 and leads Seattle's targets; Denver's corners Surtain and Moss could be out again, but their status is unconfirmed until practice reports.

detail.matchup: Surtain was projected to miss about two games after his Week 4 ankle injury, and Moss (ribs) also sat Week 5.
detail.conditions: Wind gusting near 21 mph is the main risk to his yards.

CFB-week.summary: Only three midweek Group of Five games fall in the window (Delaware at Middle Tennessee and FIU at Jacksonville State on Tuesday, Kennesaw State at Missouri State on Wednesday), all with tight spreads and totals in the 40s to low 50s. As of Monday Oct 12, none of the reputable odds or research pages checked (Covers, Action Network, FanDuel Research, RotoWire betting, Lines.com) had posted player prop lines for these games, so no lines were recorded and no picks were made.

NFL-BUF-at-LA-1013.summary: Buffalo arrives thin: WR Joshua Palmer and DT Ed Oliver are out, DJ Moore is questionable after missing Thursday and Friday practice, and the secondary is patched, with nickel Dee Alford questionable and rookie Maxwell Hairston starting. The Rams are close to full strength, with Nacua back and TE Colby Parkinson practicing fully, which cuts into Tyler Higbee's role. The total rose from 53.5 to 54.5 and the Rams are about -3 at home indoors.

NFL-SEA-at-DEN-1016.summary: Denver's starting corners are both hurt: Surtain (ankle) was given roughly a two-game absence after Week 4 and missed Week 5, and Moss (ribs) also sat. On a short week that leaves backups Abrams-Draine and Barron likely facing a Seattle passing game that runs through Smith-Njigba. Seattle again has no Charbonnet (PUP), so Emanuel Wilson carries the backfield. Denver's passing game was thin in a 23-17 win (Nix 123 yards, WR Pat Bryant hurt). Seattle opened at -1.5 with a 42.5 total, the packet's later number is 41.5, and the forecast has about 14 mph wind and a 40% chance of rain. It is…

SOCCER-day.summary: No packet player is ruled out. Livakovic is behind Joan Garcia for the Barcelona start, Forbs is struggling with a muscle injury, Osimhen has played about 19 minutes since his adductor strain, and Salech is missing from Cardiff's predicted XI. Kane, Olise and Yamal are fit, and Bayern and Barcelona each have attackers out.

fix.summary: Quick checks on six Top-10 picks: Nacua over has support, Allen rush attempts and Adams yards over draw caution, and the rest are neutral with no clear news.

NFL-BAL-at-ATL-1012.summary: Lamar Jackson (ankle) and Trey Hendrickson are out, so Tyler Huntley starts and Atlanta is about a 3-3.5-point home favorite with a 43.5 total. Zay Flowers (foot, never full in practice) is expected to play per Schefter. Atlanta's offense has turned run-first under Penix (Bijan 194 and 145 rush yards the last two weeks, five team rushing TDs vs New Orleans), and its run defense has allowed just two rushing TDs, which caps Derrick Henry.

best.why: Stafford has passed for 300 or more yards in three straight games, and Buffalo's pass defense is short-handed with DT Ed Oliver out and nickel Dee Alford questionable. The game is indoors with a total that rose to about 54.5, and a prediction market prices 275+ yards slightly above even.
